question: Does the newest-ancestor, most-chains or fewest-chains rule pick the spine matching of the ten plastic-number eddies, and is the matching forced (unique)?

public_inputs.run: scripts/longrun.py launch job.py; python3 -B merge.py <out dir> <results.json>
public_inputs.reused: JUNCTION-KINDS spinelib.py and kindlib.py (growth, ancestors, matching); BREAK-EDDIES population.json

forbidden_inputs: Changing a rule, a start, the window or a prediction after reading any frozen growth
cheapest_meaningful_control: the degree-preserving shuffle null at rounds 10, 15 and 20

predictions.S1: N never picks the spine (by count)
predictions.S4: forced share below 1 at every recurrent round from 6
predictions.S5: M's single picks collide by round 13 in at least 8 of 10

decision_rules.each: held iff no exception (S5: iff at least 8)

stop_rule: One run; read-out; referee hand-off; report.
